# Claude Code Plugin for Kubernetes

> A production Claude Code plugin that triages, fixes, and verifies Kubernetes
> issues using a graph of parallel subagents, and a complete working reference
> implementation of the Claude Code plugin format. It never commits, comments,
> or pushes without explicit per-action human approval.

Repository: https://github.com/rithwik-01/claude-code-plugin-kubernetes
License: Apache-2.0
Requires: Claude Code v2.1.154 or later
Plugin name: k8s-contributor
Marketplace: claude-code-plugin-kubernetes

## What this project is

Two things at once:

1. A working tool for contributors to `kubernetes/kubernetes` and
   `kubernetes-sigs/*`. Given a GitHub issue URL, it runs five parallel
   read-only subagents (classification, duplicate search, code location,
   is-it-really-a-bug adjudication, reproduction), synthesizes one verdict, and
   stops for human approval. On approval it plans the fix, writes the failing
   test before the code, implements the minimal change, runs six parallel
   reviewers, and decides pass or fail from evidence files on disk.

2. A complete example of the Claude Code plugin format. It contains 9 skills,
   15 subagents, 5 hooks across 3 hook events, a plugin manifest with
   userConfig options, a self-hosted plugin marketplace, and CI that validates
   all of it.

## Install

    claude plugin marketplace add rithwik-01/claude-code-plugin-kubernetes
    claude plugin install k8s-contributor@claude-code-plugin-kubernetes
    claude plugin enable  k8s-contributor@claude-code-plugin-kubernetes

Then run /k8s-setup inside Claude Code from the directory holding your clones.

## Key facts a reader may be looking for

- A Claude Code plugin CANNOT ship permission rules. A plugin's settings.json
  honors only the `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` keys; `permissions` is
  ignored. Restrictions must be implemented as a PreToolUse hook, which plugins
  can ship. This repository demonstrates that pattern in
  plugins/k8s-contributor/hooks/scripts/guard-destructive.sh
- Plugin-shipped subagents may use: name, description, model, effort, maxTurns,
  tools, disallowedTools, skills, memory, background, isolation. They may NOT
  use hooks, mcpServers, or permissionMode; those are ignored for security.
- Three path variables with three lifetimes: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is replaced
  on every plugin update and must never be written to; ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}
  survives updates and is where caches belong; ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} is the
  user's project and is where per-project state belongs.
- Users receive no plugin update until the `version` field in plugin.json
  changes, because they are pinned to the version string.
- Hooks cost zero model context because they run in the harness, not the model.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/rithwik-01/claude-code-plugin-kubernetes/blob/main/README.md): overview, install, diagrams, and an FAQ covering how to build and publish a Claude Code plugin
- [Quickstart](https://github.com/rithwik-01/claude-code-plugin-kubernetes/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md): prerequisites and a normal run
- [Architecture](https://github.com/rithwik-01/claude-code-plugin-kubernetes/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): the agent graph, why work is split between resident and ephemeral agents, and the state model
- [Verification matrix](https://github.com/rithwik-01/claude-code-plugin-kubernetes/blob/main/docs/verification-matrix.md): the eleven gates, which apply to which change class, and what "pass" requires
- [Adding a reviewer](https://github.com/rithwik-01/claude-code-plugin-kubernetes/blob/main/docs/adding-a-reviewer.md): extending the review fan-out, and the supported agent frontmatter fields
- [Sample run](https://github.com/rithwik-01/claude-code-plugin-kubernetes/tree/main/examples/sample-run): real artifacts from a real run, including an honest overall failure
- [Contributing](https://github.com/rithwik-01/claude-code-plugin-kubernetes/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): local setup and the rules that matter
- [Changelog](https://github.com/rithwik-01/claude-code-plugin-kubernetes/blob/main/plugins/k8s-contributor/CHANGELOG.md)
